content_sections.heading: About NIT Silchar
content_sections.text: National Institute of Technology Silchar is an Institute of National Importance in Silchar, Assam (PIN 788010). Its Department of ECE runs this recruitment through the Office of the Dean (Research & Consultancy). The post falls under the accelerated research for 6G ecosystem programme of the TTDF scheme of DoT.

rows.details: TARANG: Design of Terahertz Wireless Communications Systems for 6G
Developing better technologies to overcome propagation loss in the terahertz channel, and using AI to develop low-complexity beam training and resource management in wireless communication
Dr. Sucharita Chakraborty, Assistant Professor, Department of ECE, NIT Silchar, Assam-788010

content_sections.heading: NIT Silchar Junior Research Fellow Vacancy Details 2026

rows.pay: Rs. 37,000 per month (with and without GATE/NET)

content_sections.heading: NIT Silchar Junior Research Fellow Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: The maximum age is 35 years, counted on the closing date of applications, 13 November 2026. The notice prints the essential qualification as follows: Candidates with or without a valid GATE/NET who have at least 60% aggregate marks or 6.5 CGPA in both UG and PG (GEN/GEN-EWS/OBC-NCL). For SC/ST/PwD candidates, the minimum is 55% aggregate marks or 6.0 CGPA in both UG and PG. OR candidates with a Bachelor's degree in Engineering/Technology with a CGPA of at least 7.5/10 or 70% marks (GEN/GEN-EWS/OBC-NCL). For SC/ST/PwD candidates, the minimum is a CGPA of 7.0/10 or 65%. B.Tech/B.E or equivalent degree in ECE and M.Tech/M.E in ECE or equivalent, OR B.Tech/B.E or equivalent degree in ECE. This is preferred, not mandatory: a solid understanding of digital communication, probability theory, optimization and wireless communications, plus experience with programming languages such as MATLAB or Python. SC/ST/OBC/Women/PwD/EWS candidates get relaxation in qualification and age as per Government of India rules. See the official notification for the full eligibility conditions for the JRF post.

rows.event: Last date for receiving the filled application form

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Applications are screened, and the Institute may limit the number of candidates shortlisted for interview. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed. The date, the mode (online or offline) and other details will be sent by email. If no suitable candidate is found, nobody may be recruited.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The post is temporary and funded by the TARANG project. Duration: 03 years or until the project is completed, whichever is earlier. Performance is reviewed every 12 months, and any extension depends on that review. Selected candidates must sign an agreement when they join. Candidates who are already employed must submit a no-objection certificate from their employer at the interview.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for NIT Silchar Junior Research Fellow Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Download the official notification and fill in the application format (Annexure 01(A)-2). Paste a photo on it and sign the declaration. Prepare a soft copy of the filled form, your C.V. and soft copies of all supporting documents. Email them to the PI at [email protected] . Use this subject line: "Application for the post of JRF under the project TARANG/TTDF/6G/461". Send the email on or before 13 November 2026. The application form asks for: Attach a category certificate if you belong to SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD. Send questions to the same email address.

faq.question: Q1. How many JRF posts has NIT Silchar advertised?
faq.answer: One post: 01 (one) Junior Research Fellow for the TARANG project in the Department of ECE.

faq.question: Q2. Is GATE or NET compulsory?
faq.answer: No. Candidates with or without a valid GATE/NET can apply, and the pay is Rs. 37,000 a month either way.

faq.question: Q3. Can a B.Tech graduate without an M.Tech apply?
faq.answer: Yes. The notice accepts a Bachelor's degree in Engineering/Technology in ECE alone, with at least 7.5/10 CGPA or 70% marks. For SC/ST/PwD candidates, the minimum is 7.0/10 CGPA or 65%.

faq.question: Q4. What marks do candidates with both UG and PG need?
faq.answer: At least 60% aggregate or 6.5 CGPA in both UG and PG for GEN/GEN-EWS/OBC-NCL candidates. SC/ST/PwD candidates need 55% or 6.0 CGPA.

faq.question: Q5. What subject line should the application email have?
faq.answer: "Application for the post of JRF under the project TARANG/TTDF/6G/461".

faq.question: Q6. What will the JRF work on?
faq.answer: The project develops technologies to overcome terahertz channel propagation loss, and uses AI for low-complexity beam training and resource management in 6G wireless communication. TTDF/DoT, Govt. of India funds it.

faq.question: Q7. Which skills are preferred?
faq.answer: Knowledge of digital communication, probability theory, optimization and wireless communications, plus MATLAB or Python programming.

faq.question: Q8. How long is the appointment?
faq.answer: Up to 03 years or until the project closes, whichever is earlier. Any extension depends on a performance review every 12 months.

faq.question: Q9. What must an employed candidate bring to the interview?
faq.answer: A no-objection certificate from their current employer.

faq.question: Q10. Who is the Principal Investigator of the project?
faq.answer: Dr. Sucharita Chakraborty, Assistant Professor, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, NIT Silchar.
